_meta.purpose: Held-out evaluation-only probe for the mobilization-versus-sentiment confound. These seeds are not training candidates.
_meta.rule: Every event has negative surface sentiment aimed at the declared benefiting party, while backlash turnout makes that party the known-correct net beneficiary. A sentiment-only rule therefore predicts the opposite sign.
_meta.expected_delta_eff_sign: positive because each record is modeled from the benefiting party perspective

seeds.description: A Democratic administration's emergency climate regulations draw furious protests and hostile coverage, but the backlash rallies Democratic environmental voters to turn out in defense of the administration.
seeds.why_sentiment_is_wrong: Negative reaction targets Democrats, but defensive backlash turnout benefits Democrats.

seeds.description: A Republican governor's border crackdown receives angry national condemnation and street protests, but the backlash consolidates Republican voters behind the governor and raises their turnout.
seeds.why_sentiment_is_wrong: Negative reaction targets Republicans, but defensive backlash turnout benefits Republicans.

seeds.description: Hostile coverage blames a Democratic mayor for a disruptive public-sector strike; attacks on the mayor trigger labor and allied voters to mobilize defensively for Democrats.
seeds.why_sentiment_is_wrong: The negative narrative is a turnout trigger for the attacked party's coalition.

seeds.description: A Republican administration's oil-drilling decision prompts angry condemnation and viral protests, but the backlash activates Republican energy-state voters to turn out for the administration.
seeds.why_sentiment_is_wrong: Outrage aimed at Republicans produces counter-mobilization for Republicans.

seeds.description: A Democratic governor's school-curriculum directive is denounced in angry media coverage, but the attacks mobilize Democratic parents and educators to defend the governor at the polls.
seeds.why_sentiment_is_wrong: The attacked side receives the turnout gain despite hostile tone.

seeds.description: A Republican mayor's policing initiative faces furious protests and negative news coverage, but the criticism consolidates Republican public-safety voters into higher turnout for the mayor's party.
seeds.why_sentiment_is_wrong: Sentiment says Republican loss; defensive turnout says Republican gain.

seeds.description: A Democratic administration's voting-rights order is attacked in hostile coverage and mass opposition messaging, but that backlash spurs Democratic turnout to protect the order.
seeds.why_sentiment_is_wrong: Hostile tone toward Democrats causes mobilization in their favor.

seeds.description: A Republican legislature's parental-rights law is met with angry condemnation and boycott calls, but the attacks mobilize Republican supporters to defend the law through turnout.
seeds.why_sentiment_is_wrong: A negative reaction is specifically stipulated as a Republican turnout stimulus.

seeds.description: A Democratic governor's reproductive-health expansion is attacked by angry opposition campaigns, but those attacks intensify turnout among Democratic voters defending the policy.
seeds.why_sentiment_is_wrong: Surface hostility predicts a Democratic loss only if mobilization is ignored.

seeds.description: A Republican administration's gun-rights order prompts furious criticism and protest coverage, but the backlash activates Republican gun-rights supporters to turn out for the administration.
seeds.why_sentiment_is_wrong: Negative tone targets the beneficiary, while backlash turnout gives it the gain.
